children: China's yuan strengthened on Friday to a fresh 3-1/2-year high against the dollar, underpinned by broad dollar weakness, even as the central bank set the official midpoint with the largest weak bias in six months.
The spot yuan
opened at 6.7180 per dollar and was last trading at 6.7165 as of 0243 GMT, 13 pips firmer than the previous late session close, and the strongest since February 2023.
"What also helped push the dollar weaker and JPY and Asia FX stronger was Governor Waller's speech yesterday," said analysts at MUFG in a note.

Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said on Thursday he is leaning toward keeping interest rates steady at the U.S. central bank's policy meeting this month if the next batch of inflation data shows price pressures are continuing to moderate.

Market pricing for Federal Reserve rate hike expectations appears overstretched, particularly in the wake of the Jackson Hole symposium, and the dollar is likely to soften over time, the MUFG analysts said.
Prior to the market opening, the People's Bank of China set the midpoint rate

at 6.7787 per dollar. While that was the strongest fix since February 8, 2023, it was still 694 pips weaker than a Reuters estimate – the largest such deviation since late February, suggesting authorities are uncomfortable with a sharp rally in the yuan.
The spot yuan is allowed to trade 2% either side of the fixed midpoint each day.

Analysts at Nanhua Futures said domestic firms' willingness to convert dollar to yuan had eased at the margin while a wait-and-see mood was building in the market, somewhat slowing the pace of yuan appreciation. Still, they said a robust export sector and a persistent trade surplus continued to provide solid fundamental support for the currency.
They expect the currency pair to trade in a core range of around 6.69 to 6.77 in September.
The dollar index
, which measures the greenback against a basket of six currencies, was 0.035% higher at 99.
The offshore yuan traded at 6.7162 yuan per dollar
, up about 0.03% in Asian trade.
